picks.title: Breaking the Sorting Barrier for Directed Single-Source Shortest Paths
picks.abstract: We give a deterministic O (m log 2/3 n)-time algorithm for single-source shortest paths (SSSP) on directed graphs with real non-negative edge weights in the comparison-addition model. This is the first result to break the O (m+n log n) time bound of Dijkstra’s algorithm on sparse graphs, showing that Dijkstra’s algorithm is not optimal for SSSP.

picks.title: Nonadiabatic theory of phonon magnetic moments in insulators and metals
picks.abstract: We develop a nonadiabatic theory of phonon magnetic moments applicable to both insulators and metals. By relating the phonon magnetic moment to the force-velocity response of ions in a magnetic field, we derive a gauge-invariant expression using a gauge-covariant Wigner expansion. The formalism naturally separates Fermi-sea and Fermi-surface contributions and captures the full dependence on phonon frequency. In gapped systems, our theory reduces to previous adiabatic expressions in the low-frequency limit. Beyond this limit, it reveals additional contributions arising from resonant interband processes and the Fermi surface. Applying our theory to Pb 1 − x Sn x Te, we find that the Fermi-surface contribution substantially enhances the phonon magnetic moment, reproducing the same order of magnitude as the experimental observation. Our results provide a unified framework for describing phonon magnetic moments beyond the adiabatic regime.

picks.title: Plasma waveguides for high-intensity laser pulses
picks.abstract: Fundamental to many applications of laser pulses in science and technology is an extended interaction length with matter that significantly exceeds the distance over which the pulse would normally diffract and transversely spread. At low intensity, the interaction could simply be the linear refraction provided by a glass optical fiber to keep the pulse from spreading. At higher pulse intensities, however, the goal extends beyond diffraction-free pulse transport: an extended interaction length of high intensity light can give rise to bright secondary sources of photons and, at relativistic intensities, beams of high energy charged particles. Since these applications require laser intensities well above the threshold for ionization of atoms, new methods for overcoming pulse diffraction in a plasma have been developed. Chief among them are plasma waveguides  optical fibers composed of plasma, with characteristic mode structure. This article reviews the methods and theory of plasma waveguides, highlighting the recent development of meter-scale plasma waveguides that have been instrumental to the laser acceleration of high-charge electron beams to energies ~10 GeV.

picks.title: Mapping Dust Attenuation at Kiloparsec Scales. III. The 2175 Å Bump
picks.abstract: We combine the Swift/UVOT+MaNGA catalog with Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) K s imaging to map the 2175 Å attenuation bump at kiloparsec scales in nearby galaxies. We use two complementary estimators: an ultraviolet-to-near-infrared attenuation-curve method, yielding A bump UOIR and B for 2487 high-continuum-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) spaxels, and the near-ultraviolet-only method of A. Battisti et al., yielding A bump NUV and k bump for 7934 spaxels. The two absolute bump estimates agree well where they overlap. We compare bump strength with local stellar-population, emission-line, attenuation-curve, and geometric diagnostics after separating star-forming (SF) and non-SF regions. The strongest bumps occur at low specific H α surface brightness, Σ H α /Σ *, especially in non-SF regions, where this ratio traces ionized-gas emission per unit stellar mass rather than sSFR. The bump also weakens with EW(H α) and strengthens with D n 4000 and stellar age. In contrast, metallicity, inclination, galactocentric radius, A V, and optical attenuation-curve slope are secondary predictors. The absolute strength A bump NUV increases with Σ H α and Σ *, while the relative strengths k bump and B do not, indicating that absolute bump amplitude partly follows dust column whereas normalized strengths better trace effective bump prominence. These results support local radiation-field processing of the 2175 Å carriers.

picks.title: A Warped Dust Ring in the CQ Tau Disk
picks.abstract: The diversity of planetary orbital architectures calls for observational constraints on radial variations in disk-plane orientation, or warps, yet such variations in dust disks remain poorly characterized. CQ Tau is a promising target because its misaligned inner disk and candidate gas warp suggest a radially extended warp. We present the ALMA 1.3 mm dust continuum image reconstructed from the real part of the visibilities, extracting the centro-symmetric disk structure. At an effective spatial resolution of 0. ″ 052 × 0. ″ 042 (7.8 × 6.3 au), the image reveals a bright main ring at radii of ∼20–70 au and an unresolved compact emission component tracing the inner disk around the central star. Ellipse fits centered on the stellar position to contours tracing the inner and outer edges of the ring reveal radial variations in position angles and inclinations. At the inner edge (∼21–26 au), the position angle and inclination span 214 ∘ –233 ∘ and 23 ∘ –39 ∘, respectively, while they span 231 ∘ –235 ∘ and 33 ∘ –36 ∘ at the outer edge (∼58–67 au). Whereas a coplanar ring toy model fails to reproduce such variations, a warped ring model with the local tilt decreasing from ∼4 ∘ at r = 20 au to ∼1 ∘ at 60 au reproduces them. The high-pass-filtered real-part image reveals a pair of opposed curved negative residuals. Similar features appear only in the warped ring model, further supporting the dust warp. These results establish CQ Tau as an example of a warped dust disk and an important laboratory for investigating the connection between three-dimensional disk geometry and planet formation.

picks.title: STIR: Reed–Solomon Proximity Testing with Fewer Queries
picks.abstract: We present STIR (Shift To Improve Rate), an interactive oracle proof of proximity (IOPP) for Reed–Solomon codes that achieves the best known query complexity of any concretely efficient IOPP for this problem. For λ bits of security, STIR has query complexity O (log d + λ ⋅ loglog d), while FRI, a popular protocol, has query complexity O (λ ⋅ log d) (including variants of FRI based on conjectured security assumptions). STIR relies on a new technique for recursively improving the rate of the tested Reed–Solomon code. We provide an implementation of STIR compiled to a SNARK. Compared to a highly-optimized implementation of FRI, STIR achieves an improvement in argument size that ranges from 1.25× to 2.46× depending on the chosen parameters, with similar prover and verifier running times. For example, in order to achieve 128 bits of security for degree 2 26 and rate 1/4, STIR has argument size 114 KiB, compared to 211 KiB for FRI.

picks.title: Nanoscale Flexibility Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative Water Sorption
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Passive, sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting technologies (AWHTs) have attracted recent interest as an alternative to energy-intensive condensation-based technologies. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer wide chemical tunability to design sorbents, but in practice, sorbents must retain moisture during humidity fluctuations, and small adsorption enthalpies are necessary for regeneration of the sorbent material. Here, we report that Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles with diameters less than 120 nm exhibit structural flexibility at the Cu2+ centers that enables a “breathing”-type cooperative water sorption. This cooperative structural phase change occurs only for nanoparticles that contain Cu2+, and not for the isomorphic magnesium triazolate. The phase change significantly decreases the onset pressures of adsorption and desorption compared to large particles and opens a practically useful hysteresis window in the isotherms, while maintaining small adsorption enthalpies (48 kJ/mol averaged over the isotherm, approaching the 44 kJ/mol latent heat of water at low RH). Mechanistic analysis indicates that adsorption initiates with weak electrostatic and dispersion interactions between water and triazolate rings brought into close proximity only by the distorted Cu2+ centers of the nanoparticles. Together, these results present a distinct water sorption mechanism and design strategy that leverages size- and metal-dependent lattice flexibility in a wide class of porous materials.

picks.title: Resolving Chlorine Sites in Pharmaceuticals by Integrated Site-Resolved Zeeman-Perturbed NQR, Solid-State NMR, and Electron Diffraction Crystallography
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and high-value chemicals feature covalently bonded chlorine functionalities that influence molecular packing, stability, and bioavailability. However, site-resolved structural characterization of chlorine sites in powders remains challenging, especially in systems with multiple chemically or crystallographically nonequivalent sites, disorder, or hydration sensitivity. We report here a novel combined 35Cl nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR), 35Cl Zeeman-perturbed NQR (Zp-NQR), 35Cl solid-state NMR, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED/microcrystal electron diffraction) approach to characterizing powdered chlorine-bearing chemicals. Case studies of ketoconazole and chloramine-T demonstrate the utility of the approach in characterizing local structural heterogeneity and the hydration state. The role of crystal packing and noncovalent interactions on the spectroscopic observables is provided through an analysis of chlorzoxazone and five of its cocrystals, of which three are novel. Compared to ultrahigh-field NMR spectra alone, NQR and Zp-NQR spectra provide improved sensitivity to small changes in the electric field gradient and in the degree of disorder around chlorine. Experimental NQR/Zp-NQR data combined with gauge-including projector augmented-wave density functional theory (GIPAW-DFT) provide local structural constraints for a partially dehydrated chloramine-T phase. The refinement protocol does not require single crystals, and in the case of NQR experiments, intact tablets containing APIs are analyzed directly without further treatment or grinding. As a proof of principle, commercial tablets are shown to contain ketoconazole in the same crystalline form as that seen for the pure API. The general approach…

picks.title: Screening for Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
picks.abstract: Background: Previous reviews on prostate cancer screening relied on ongoing trials of invitations to screening with prostate-specific antigen (PSA), which may lack sufficient follow-up for mortality and overdiagnosis. Other screening tests with higher specificity may improve the benefit–harm profile. Purpose: To examine benefits and harms of screening versus no screening or usual care. Data Sources: MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (2014 to 28 January 2026); reviews and included studies for studies published before 2014. Study Selection: Paired reviewers identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective nonrandomized studies. Benefit outcomes relied on data reported by age when possible. Data Extraction: Paired reviewers extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted with investigation of heterogeneity; assessment of certainty of evidence used the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach with decision thresholds as the targets of certainty. Data Synthesis: Thirteen RCTs ( n = 792 034; 8 from a multisite European trial, and 1 for harms only) and 3 uncontrolled cohort studies ( n = 5593; all for harms) were included. All RCTs compared invitations to PSA-based screening versus no invitation. At 20 years’ follow-up, among 1000 men who were invited to multiple rounds of PSA-based screening every 2 to 4 years starting at age 55 to 69 years (mean, 62 years), there was likely a reduction in prostate cancer mortality (≥2 fewer) and metastatic cancer incidence (≥6 fewer) at the expense of prostate cancer overdiagnosis (≥20 cases) and false positives (≥150 cases) (all moderate certainty). Findings for ages 50 to 54 years were less certain. An invitation…

picks.title: Carbon home bias
picks.abstract: We undertake a global analysis of institutional investor portfolios and find widespread underweighting of companies with higher carbon emissions, both in levels and intensities. This underweighting is largely driven by foreign companies with high carbon emissions, both at the intensive (tilting) and extensive (exclusion) margins. Domestic firms with high emissions are overweighted but by a smaller magnitude. These results reveal a bias for domestic companies with high carbon emissions. The carbon home bias is stronger in settings where institutions have tighter business connections, in countries with weaker social norms regarding climate crisis, and where the political environment is more polarized.

more.title: Probing the Memory of a Superconducting Qubit Environment
more.abstract: Achieving fault tolerance with superconducting quantum processors requires qubits to operate within the regime of threshold theorems based on the Born-Markov approximation. This approximation, which models dissipation as constant energy decay into a memoryless environment, breaks down when qubits couple to long-lived two-level systems (TLSs) that become polarized during operation and retain memory of past qubit states. Here, we show that non-Poissonian quantum jump traces carry the information required to distinguish long-lived TLSs from the standard Markovian bath. By fitting the Solomon equations to measured quantum jump dynamics arising naturally from thermal fluctuations, we can disentangle the qubit’s coupling to the two environments. Sweeping the qubit frequency reveals distinct peaks, each associated with a TLS that outlives the qubit, providing a handle to understand their microscopic origin.

more.title: Separability of the motion of spinning test particles in curved space-time
more.abstract: Solving for the motion of spinning test particles in curved spacetimes is important for modeling gravitational-wave inspirals of spinning compact binaries. We build a Hamiltonian formalism in worldline-adapted frames for the spinning test particle and formulate a corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi equation valid to linear order in spin. We prove that when the geodesic motion in a spacetime and the parallel transport along said geodesics are both separable, then so is the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The key insight is that the transform to the worldline-adapted frame that separates parallel transport also coincidentally generates a near-identity transform into separation coordinates in the orbital sector. We illustrate this in black hole, plane wave, and cosmological spacetimes.

more.title: Optimal discrimination of Gaussian states by Gaussian measurements
more.abstract: Are Gaussian measurements enough to distinguish between Gaussian states? Here, we tackle this question by focusing on the max-relative entropy as an operational distinguishability metric. Given two multimode Gaussian states ρ , σ with covariance matrices V σ > V ρ , we derive a condition that completely determines whether or not there exists an optimal Gaussian measurement achieving the max-relative entropy. When the condition is satisfied, we find this optimal measurement explicitly. When the condition is not met, there is a strict gap between the distinguishability achievable by Gaussian measurements and the unconstrained max-relative entropy in which all measurements are allowed. We illustrate our results in the single-mode setting, and show examples of states for which this gap can be made arbitrarily large, revealing novel instances of Gaussian data hiding.

more.title: MeerKAT thousand-pulsar polarization array: Searches for ultralight axionlike dark matter
more.abstract: We construct Pulsar Polarisation Arrays (PPA), using regular pulsars monitored in MeerKAT’s Thousand Pulsar Array (TPA) Programme, to search for Axion-like Dark Matter (ALDM) within Milky Way. Specifically, from a catalogue of 1237 regular pulsars, we select the 50 ones with the highest signal-to-noise ratio and set upper limits on the ALDM Chern-Simons coupling. We find no signals with statistical significance over the mass range of [ 10 − 23 , 10 − 20 ] e V in the six-year MeerKAT’s data. By combining the high-quality TPA pulsars and the accurate ionospheric subtraction of , we establish the most sensitive upper limits to the date on the ALDM Chern-Simons coupling, namely ≲ 10 − 14 − 3 × 10 − 13 GeV − 1 , for the mass range of [ 10 − 23 , 10 − 21 ] e V except at m a ≃ 1.3 × 10 − 22 eV. This study highlights the great promise of regular-pulsar PPAs, whose large population and flexible design open a powerful new window on fundamental physics with next-generation radio telescopes.

more.title: Whistler Wave Generation from Lower-hybrid Turbulence in Solar Flares: Implications for Radio Fiber Bursts
more.abstract: We report the identification of whistler wave generation by ion-ring-driven lower-hybrid (LH) turbulence in solar flare plasma environments using fully kinetic two-dimensional (2D) particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. While previous studies established that ion rings excite LH waves capable of accelerating electrons to hard X-ray (HXR) energies, the generation of secondary whistler waves—required to explain radio fiber bursts—remains unresolved. We contrast two regimes at a fixed ring velocity v r: a sub-Alfvénic (v r < V A) case (δ = ω pe /Ω ce = 0.5) and a super-Alfvénic (v r > V A) case (δ = 5.0). In the sub-Alfvénic case, the ring-driven instability is initially electrostatic. LH waves reach large amplitudes and accelerate electrons to 20–100 keV, capable of producing HXR emission. Crucially, whistler waves subsequently emerge via nonlinear wave–particle scattering. Conversely, in the super-Alfvénic case, the system is forced into an electromagnetic regime. Here, whistlers are directly and linearly excited—evidenced by the simultaneous exponential growth of electric and magnetic fluctuations. However, electron Landau damping restricts the wave spectrum to a limited range of small parallel wavenumbers, reducing parallel electron acceleration (≲10 keV). By capturing the kinetic transition from the sub- to the super-Alfvénic regime, these idealized limits suggest a microscopic framework for the established model of solar flares: ion-ring drivers could self-consistently power both HXR-producing electrons in dense footpoints and the whistler populations required for radio fiber bursts in weaker-field coronal exhausts.

more.title: The Contribution of Starspots to the Lithium Spread in NGC 2264
more.abstract: Star clusters with ages of a few Myr have a previously unexplained dispersion in the lithium equivalent widths. In this work, we show that much of the lithium spread of the young cluster NGC 2264 can be attributed to the observational presence of starspots. We demonstrate that the equivalent width of Li i 6708 Å changes with observed spot coverage, using a sample of 15 Weak-Lined T Tauri Stars (WTTSs) with multiepoch high-resolution ESPaDOnS spectra and photometry. To quantify the contribution of starspots, we construct an empirical two-component starspot model. When differences in visible spot coverage are taken into account, 68% of the WTTSs fall within the model-predicted EW(Li) dispersion for a range from 0% to 90% visible spot coverage. We find no correlation between the age spread or gravity and Li i equivalent width in NGC 2264. Our results suggest that invoking starspots can explain much of the apparent lithium spread in NGC 2264 and reduces but does not fully eliminate the need to invoke rotation-driven lithium depletion or other nonstandard explanations at such young ages. Future simultaneous measurements of lithium and beryllium in young stars may provide an independent test of this scenario.

more.title: Sequential Star Formation and the Near-infrared Stellar Populations within N159
more.abstract: We present the first results from a JWST/NIRCam study of the star-forming region N159, one of the richest H ii complexes in the Large Magellanic Cloud. This region stretches over ∼130 pc, and exemplifies large-scale sequential star formation. We present photometric results of >300,000 point sources combining data from 10 near-infrared JWST filters spanning 1–4.7 μ m. We detect sources as faint as ∼27 mag at F115W, corresponding to stellar masses reaching below ∼0.1 M ⊙. By constructing several color–magnitude and color–color diagrams, we separate young stars from main-sequence and older stars within N159, finding evidence for stellar populations younger than 0.5 Myr. Of the young population, we identify accreting, pre-main-sequence stars from their Paschen- α (Pa α) excess and a population of sources bearing strong infrared (IR) excess, representing candidate young stellar objects (YSOs). Within this population, we identify a subpopulation of sources with H 2 O ice absorption. The IR-excess-bearing YSO candidates correlate spatially with dust filaments and molecular gas demonstrating their embedded state. The distribution of stellar and candidate YSO populations across N159 reveals more evolved star-forming populations in the N159E region and newer star formation in the N159W region, supporting the sequential star formation scenario for this region.

more.title: G:C:G:C-Flanked i-Motifs Are Thermodynamically Favored and Their Sequences Highly Enriched in the Human Genome
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: i-Motifs are biologically relevant noncanonical DNA structures whose stability is strongly influenced by capping interactions. Among these, minor groove tetrads (MGTs) are among the most powerful stabilizing elements identified to date, yet the molecular factors governing their effects and their potential biological significance remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic experimental and computational analysis of 16 MGT-stabilized i-motifs (MGTiMs), encompassing all combinations of terminal tetrad composition and orientation within a common sequence scaffold. NMR spectroscopy confirms that all sequences adopt closely related architectures, enabling direct comparison of the effects of tetrad identity and orientation on stability. Thermal denaturation experiments reveal that the stability hierarchy, previously observed in selected structures (G:C:G:C ≳ G:C:G:T ≫ G:T:G:T), is broadly maintained across the series, although substantial positional effects are observed. Molecular dynamics simulations and energy decomposition analyses suggest that differences in electrostatic interactions and local conformational flexibility contribute to these trends. Notably, genome-wide analysis of the human genome reveals a strong enrichment of sequences capable of forming the most stabilizing tetrads, with motifs containing two G:C:G:C tetrads reaching a 45-fold enrichment relative to random expectation. Interestingly, this most abundant genomic motif is also the only one that undergoes pronounced pH-driven conformational transitions, highlighting the unique structural plasticity of these architectures. Together, these findings reveal how tetrad composition and positional context govern MGTiM stability and identify NN-type motifs as a particularly enriched class of…

more.title: Revisiting the Role of Global Magnetic Variables in Coronal Heating of Solar Active Regions
more.abstract: Reconnection-based models of coronal heating predict that magnetic complexity—nonpotential configurations, currents, and shear—should enhance coronal emission independently of total magnetic flux. Previous work using Yohkoh soft X-ray observations and ground-based vector magnetograms, however, found no evidence that complexity contributes independently to coronal heating. We revisit this question using Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)/Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) vector magnetograms and SDO/Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) EUV imaging. HMI Space-weather Active Region Patch (SHARP) provide 16 magnetic parameters characterizing field strength, gradients, currents, helicity, and nonpotentiality. We measure spatially integrated transition region and coronal emission using AIA 304Å, 193Å, 94 Å, and isolated Fe xviii emission for 137 active regions, sampling plasma at ∼0.09, ∼1.4, and ∼7.1 MK. Partial correlation analysis isolates the contribution of each complexity parameter after controlling for total unsigned vertical magnetic flux. Unsigned flux (Φ M) explains 72%–82% of variance in emission, following power laws (I ∝ Φ M α, where α = 0.61–1.19) consistent with prior soft X-ray results. Partial correlations reveal weak positive contributions (r = 0.2–0.3) to transition region (304 Å) emission from some vertical current and field parameters but little evidence that other active-region-averaged measures of magnetic complexity enhance coronal emission. The exception is total photospheric magnetic free energy density (ρ tot), which shows a positive partial correlation (r = 0.49, p < 0.001) with Fe xviii emission, but negative, or nonexistent, partial correlations with other AIA filters. more.title: Extremal Fitting Problems for Conjunctive Queries
more.abstract: The fitting problem for conjunctive queries (CQs) is the problem to construct a CQ that fits a given set of labeled data examples. When a fitting CQ exists, it is in general not unique. This leads us to propose natural refinements of the notion of a fitting CQ, such as most-general fitting CQ, most-specific fitting CQ, and unique fitting CQ. We give structural characterizations of these notions in terms of (suitable refinements of) homomorphism dualities, frontiers, and direct products, which enable the construction of the refined fitting CQs when they exist. We also pinpoint the complexity of the associated existence and verification problems, and determine the size of fitting CQs. We study the same problems for unions of CQs (UCQs).

more.title: A Unique Conformationally Assisted [2+2] Configuration in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Two π-conjugated macrocycles, namely the well-known [12]cycloparaphenylene and a newly designed macrocycle combining benzenes and rigid stilbene units, are presented for the first time as light-amplifying gain media in distributed feedback (DFB) laser devices. Both systems show good photonic functionality arising from a four-state photonic cycle comprising a [2+2] state configuration (two delocalized and two conformationally distorted localized states). The mechanism involves the generation of two optically coupled states through excited-state structural distortion induced during internal conversion, which reduces light reabsorption losses and promotes rapid population inversion. Comprehensive steady-state absorption and fluorescence and transient absorption spectroscopy studies are conducted in order to reveal the nature of the low energy lying excited states. Furthermore, amplified spontaneous emission studies of the compounds in polystyrene thin films, followed by the preparation and characterization of optically pumped DFB lasers, were performed. The results reveal new properties of these multifunctional cyclic π-conjugated molecules and unique structure-property relationships.
more.topic: Synthesis and Properties of Aromatic Compounds

more.title: An Allosteric CLR N-Terminal Swing-Out Mechanism for RAMP-Mediated Adrenomedullin Receptor Selectivity
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Three receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMP1–3) form heterodimers with the calcitonin (CTR) and calcitonin-like (CLR) G protein-coupled receptors and determine their selectivity for six CGRP family peptide agonists. These ligand–receptor systems are drug targets for migraine headache, diabetes and obesity, and circulatory system disorders. Here, we used molecular dynamics simulations and pharmacological assays of receptor chimeras and point mutants to identify a crucial allosteric component of the mechanism by which RAMP2 and RAMP3 modulate CLR to confer selectivity for two adrenomedullin (AM) peptides. We found that the extracellular domain (ECD) of RAMP2 and RAMP3, but not RAMP1, stabilized a partially unwound “swing-out” conformation of the CLR ECD N-terminal α-helix to accommodate the unique binding mode of the midregion of the AM peptides. The inability of the CTR N-terminus to adopt the swing-out conformation contributed to the distinct peptide selectivity profile of the three CTR-RAMP amylin receptors. By exploiting the CLR swing-out conformation, we engineered AM antagonist peptide variants with enhanced affinity and selectivity for CLR-RAMP2 and -RAMP3. Our results reveal the long-sought mechanism of RAMP-altered CLR ligand selectivity and have significant implications for drug development targeting the CLR- and CTR-RAMP complexes.

more.title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe 2–x Te x Polytypic Heterostructures
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure–superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2–xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range─from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T′ structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8) shows suppressed Tc (∼2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin–orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.

more.title: The Complexity of Subgame-perfect Equilibria in Parity and Mean-payoff Games
more.abstract: In this article, we prove that the SPE constrained existence problem, i.e., the problem of deciding, in a given game, the existence of a subgame-perfect equilibrium that generates a payoff profile between two given thresholds, is NP-complete for both parity games and mean-payoff games. For that purpose, we use the notion of negotiation function, and the fact that a play is compatible with an SPE if and only if it is consistent with a fixed point of that function. Our algorithms consist in guessing (1) such a fixed point, (2) a certificate of the existence of a play consistent with that fixed point that matches the constraints, and (3) a certificate proving that it is a fixed point.

more.title: Movies’ Content Features Predict the Personalities of Their Fans
more.abstract: Movies are a central form of entertainment and cultural expression, yet little is known about how their content aligns with the psychological traits of their audiences. We link movie characteristics and contents with the aggregate Big Five personalities of social-media users from a large, international sample who “liked” them. Movie content, captured by text keywords, predicts aggregate audience personalities beyond genre, demographics, and attributes like quality and popularity. An online experiment (N = 1,018 adults) demonstrates that these content-based personality predictions are behaviorally relevant for choices and evaluations involving new movies and participants. We further provide fine-grained mappings between personality and movie features, including quality, popularity, genre, psychological themes, and unique concepts. Our findings reveal systematic links between personality and movie preferences, showing that people favor content that resonates with their thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. This research enables scalable, automated audience psychographic assessment based on content features, offering insights into personality-driven media preferences.

more.title: The potential of nanosized zeolites in catalysis
more.abstract: Zeolites with well-defined microporous frameworks are among the most widely utilized heterogeneous catalysts in petroleum refining, fine chemical synthesis, and environmental protection. However, the intrinsic diffusion limitations associated with conventional micron-sized crystals often restrict catalytic efficiency, product selectivity, and catalyst lifetime, particularly in reactions involving bulky molecules. Reducing zeolite crystal dimensions to the nanoscale has emerged as an effective strategy to alleviate transport constraints, increase external surface area, and tailor the distribution and accessibility of acid sites. As a result, nanosized zeolites have attracted significant attention as advanced catalytic materials with enhanced activity, selectivity, and stability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in nanosized zeolites, with particular emphasis on the relationship between crystal size, diffusion phenomena, acidity, and catalytic performance. The discussion is organized according to the most industrially relevant framework topologies, including 12-membered-ring zeolites (FAU, *BEA, MOR, and LTL), 10-membered-ring zeolites (MFI, FER, MWW, and MEL), and the 8-membered-ring zeolite (CHA). Each topology is critically analyzed individually, while comparative summaries are provided to highlight key structural and catalytic trends. Diverse nanoscale architectures including aggregated and monodispersed nanoparticles, self-pillared and intergrown structures, intra-crystalline mesoporous systems, finned morphologies, and nanosheets are examined to illustrate how structural design governs diffusion pathways and catalytic behavior. more.title: Nanotechnology Meets Brain Diseases: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies for Drug Delivery
more.abstract: Brain diseases, encompassing neurodegenerative disorders, cerebrovascular diseases, and brain tumors, impose a profound global health burden. Conventional therapeutic strategies often fail due to the formidable blood–brain barrier (BBB) and complex pathological microenvironment of the central nervous system (CNS). The rapid evolution of nanotechnology offers unprecedented opportunities to overcome these delivery hurdles. This review comprehensively summarizes recent developments in engineered nanoplatforms for the diagnosis and targeted therapy of brain diseases. It first outlines the pathological characteristics and nanoprobe-enhanced diagnostic methods for various brain disorders, followed by a critical evaluation of five major classes of nanocarriers for CNS drug delivery: lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, bio-derived, and hybrid nanocarriers. This evaluation highlights their structural attributes and delivery efficiencies. The discussion then examines advanced strategies to improve delivery precision, including multilevel targeting (e.g., BBB penetration and specific cell targeting), stimuli-responsive theranostics, and functional surface modifications. Linking these nanotechnological innovations to specific neurological diseases highlights their clinical potential. Finally, the review addresses current translational challenges, including biosafety, scalable manufacturing, and interindividual variability, and offers a forward-looking perspective on the rational design of next-generation precision neuro-nanomedicines.

more.title: Generative AI And Creative Goods: Market Expansion, Crowd-Out, and Copyright
more.abstract: We study how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) affects creative goods markets using data from a large stock images marketplace. In December 2022, the platform announced it would allow artists to sell GenAI-produced images, subject to two conditions: all GenAI images must be labeled, and GenAI would be prohibited in certain markets. We exploit this policy variation using a difference-in-differences design. We estimate a 136% increase in image production and 47% increase in active artists, accompanied by a 15% decline in non-GenAI production and 29% decline in non-GenAI active artists. On the demand side, total sales increase by 82%, but non-GenAI sales fall by 28% and non-GenAI sales rates decline by 3 percentage points. We use image embeddings to develop novel measures of image quality, characteristics, and market composition.We find that quality (measured as predicted sales probability) increases by 9 percentage points overall and 2 percentage points for non-GenAI content, suggesting low-quality non-GenAI artists exit. Our product characteristic measures indicate that GenAI production is heavily concentrated in characteristic space, potentially limiting the value of these images to the market. Non-GenAI production responds to GenAI by differentiating into niches. We discuss implications for copyright policy and the longer-run sustainability of original creative work.

more.title: Layered superlattices: from physical assembly to chemical synthesis and emerging applications
more.abstract: Quantum materials offer a powerful platform for exploring emergent condensed matter phenomena and developing functional devices, owing to their tunable electronic structures, quasiparticle excitations and collective quantum effects. Layered superlattices are a class of layered heterostructures formed by the periodic stacking of two or more sublattices along the direction perpendicular to the layers, with the constituent layers differing in composition, structure, or electronic properties. Such structural versatility establishes layered superlattices as a materials platform for connecting emergent quantum states with functional implementation. This review systematically summarizes the classification of sublattices in layered superlattices, including systems composed of inorganic sublattices and hybrid architectures comprising organic components and coordination-complex building blocks. It then discusses the major fabrication strategies, ranging from physical assembly to chemical synthesis, with an emphasis on the material compatibility, structural controllability and scalability of each approach. The review examines how quantum confinement, resonant tunneling, interlayer coupling and cooperative interfacial effects govern emergent physical properties and device performance. Recent progress in superconductivity, thermoelectrics, optoelectronic detection, sensing, and energy storage and conversion is also summarized. Finally, this review discusses key challenges in structural control, scalable synthesis, stability improvement, dynamic characterization and nonequilibrium photophysics, while highlighting future opportunities enabled by machine learning, high-throughput experimentation, multiscale simulations and advanced characterization. more.title: Universal small-scale fluctuation spectrum of Vlasov-Poisson turbulence
more.abstract: The thermal' fluctuation spectrum of the electric field arising due to particle noise in a quiescent Vlasov--Poisson plasma was derived in the 1960s. Here, we derive the universal fluctuation spectrum of the electric field, at Debye and sub-Debye scales, for a turbulent Vlasov--Poisson plasma. This spectrum arises from what is likely to be the final cascade’—a universal regime to be encountered at the extreme small-scale end of any turbulent cascade in a nearly collisionless plasma. The cascaded invariant is the generalized (negative) entropy C 2 , which is the quadratic Casimir invariant of the particle distribution function. C 2 cascades to small scales in both position and velocity space via both linear and nonlinear phase mixing, in such a way that the timescales associated with the two processes are `critically balanced’ at every scale. We construct a phenomenological scaling theory of the fluctuation spectrum of C 2 in ( k , s ) space—and hence of the electric field in k space—in arbitrary dimensions, where k and s are the spatial and velocity wavenumbers, respectively. The electric-field spectrum is sufficiently steep for the nonlinear mixing to be controlled by the largest-scale electric fluctuations, and so the C 2 cascade resembles the Batchelor cascade of a passive scalar, albeit in the kinetic phase space. The conclusions of our theory are corroborated by direct numerical simulations of a forced 1D-1V plasma. We predict that the cascade is ultimately terminated at the (spatial) wavenumber where the turbulent electric-field spectrum gives way to the fluctuation spectrum associated with discrete particle noise; this transition scale is set by the amplitude of the turbulent electric fields and the plasma parameter. Reconstructing the Full Kinematic Dependence of GPDs from Pseudo-Distributions
more.abstract: We propose a reconstruction of the full (x, ξ, t) dependence of unpolarized isovector proton generalized parton distributions (GPDs) H u − d and E u − d from lattice QCD data in the pseudo-distribution formalism. For the first time, we extract double distributions (DDs) directly from lattice data, therefore enforcing an important property of GPDs linked to Lorentz symmetry. We use the flexible framework of multidimensional Gaussian process regression to regularize the inverse problem and present an assessment of the impact of model dependence on the systematic uncertainty. Our lattice ensemble corresponds to a pion mass m π = 358 MeV and a lattice spacing a = 0.094 fm. We use larger hadron momenta, up to 2.7 GeV, and kinematic coverage compared to our previous computations, and extract additional skewness-dependent moments of the GPD.

Widely Used Measures of Overconfidence Are Confounded with Ability
more.abstract: Measures of overconfidence are used both to assess biases in people’s beliefs regarding their own abilities and to identify correlates of those biases. Proposed correlates of overconfidence include narcissism, social status, (low) task anxiety, savings, planning, and many more. Research on these correlates typically explicitly or implicitly claims that the associations with overconfidence are not attributable to ability (i.e., latent inputs enabling successful task performance, including inputs that vary across people, states, or contexts). I argue that several typical approaches used to measure overconfidence are not sufficient to support such claims. This argument follows from two underappreciated properties of these measures of overconfidence. First, performance is an imperfect measure of ability: accounting for performance does not sufficiently account for ability. Second, self-evaluations of performance should reflect ability in addition to performance: because performance is ambiguous, people should incorporate prior beliefs about their ability. These properties imply that multiple commonly used measures of overconfidence are confounded with ability. I support these analytical results by reexamining previously published findings. In the first analysis, I find that overconfidence predicts subsequent performance, consistent with measures of overconfidence serving as a signal of ability. In the second set of analyses, I find that some purported associations between overconfidence and other constructs could be attributed to ability instead. I close with recommendations to recognize and reduce the potential for mistaken inferences. more.title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates
more.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
more.abstract: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client-scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client-scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client-scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue-resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach for partitioning can be extended to other biomolecules, offering a framework to analyze their partitioning in cellular environments.

more.title: Determinants of Norm Compliance: Moral Similarity and Group Identification
more.abstract: What determines whether someone complies with a social norm? The social identity approach offers a mechanism for norm compliance: A person who feels similar to a group identifies more with that group and, in turn, complies with the group’s norms. Using an experiment, we test whether similarity in values increases identification and adherence to a group rule. To do so, we varied the similarity/dissimilarity between the values of an individual and members of a social group and measured group identification and rule compliance. We find that moral similarity in progressivism increases group identification, and group identification can increase compliance with rules from the social group. However, our results also suggest that this relationship can be disrupted. Because of our design and empirically verified in our study, social norms do not differ between treatments. As a consequence, observed behavior changes are attributable to increased group norm sensitivity and not changes in group norms. We advance the study of social identity by testing a causal pathway between group identification, group norm sensitivity, and behavior change. Our contribution to the management literature is to extend the empirical rationale, and cautionary notes, for investing in value-alignment between individuals and organizations. more.title: Spectroscopic Evidence of Competing Diagonal Spin Interactions and Spin Disproportionation in the Bilayer Nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7
more.abstract: A comprehensive spectroscopic map of the electronic, magnetic, and lattice excitations is presented for the bilayer nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7 using Raman scattering at ambient pressure. Upon entering the spin density wave state below 153 K, the A 1 g channel exhibits an abrupt electronic spectral gap with a clear isosbestic point. In contrast, the B 1 g and B 2 g channels are dominated by pronounced two-magnon (2M) excitations, representing a signature of incipient Mottness. These 2M signals in both channels constitute evidence for two distinct in-plane spin-exchange interactions along the Ni—O bonding and its diagonal directions. Calculations based on the spin wave theory further reveal that the 2M mode in the B 2 g channel arises from the competition between two bond-diagonal antiferromagnetic interactions mediated by nickel d x 2 − y 2 orbitals. Furthermore, emergent low-energy 2M excitations below 10 meV are found to originate from distinct, weaker spin moments, supporting spin disproportionation. Simultaneously, an anomalous softening of B 1 g phonons from 280 down to 4.5 K is uncovered, suggesting the presence of an incipient lattice instability leading to checkerboard-type breathing modulations. Collectively, these findings identify a ground state of the bilayer nickelate characterized by competing bond-diagonal interactions, spin disproportionation, and an incipient lattice instability, establishing key ingredients for understanding the mechanism of nickelate superconductivity.

more.title: Distinct mechanisms underlying in-context learning in transformers
more.abstract: Modern distributed networks, notably transformers, acquire a remarkable ability (termed in-context learning) to adapt their computation to input statistics, such that a fixed network can be applied to data from a broad range of systems. Here, we provide a complete mechanistic characterization of this behavior in transformers trained on a finite set 𝒮 of discrete Markov chains. The transformer displays four algorithmic phases, characterized by whether the network memorizes and generalizes, and whether it uses 1-point or 2-point statistics. We show that the four phases are implemented by multi-layer subcircuits that exemplify two qualitatively distinct mechanisms for implementing context-adaptive computations. Minimal models isolate the key features of both motifs. Memorization and generalization phases are delineated by two boundaries that depend on data diversity, K = | 𝒮 | . The first ( K 1 * ) is set by a kinetic competition between subcircuits and the second ( K 2 * ) is set by a representational bottleneck. A symmetry-constrained theory of a transformer's training dynamics explains the sharp transition from 1-point to 2-point generalization and identifies key features of the loss landscape that allow the network to generalize. Put together, we show that transformers develop distinct subcircuits to implement in-context learning and identify conditions that favor certain mechanisms over others.

more.title: Two new highly scattered fast radio bursts: evidence for scatter broadening by the circumsource medium
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We found two highly scattered Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) during commissioning of the Commensal Realtime ASKAP Fast Transient COherent (CRACO) backend. FRB 240210D and FRB 240312D have scattering times of 34 ± 6 and 300 ± 48 ms, respectively, when scaled to 1 GHz. FRB 240312D originates near a spiral arm of a face-on galaxy at a redshift of only 0.05. Scintillation from a Milky Way screen constrains the distance of the scattering screen to ∼10 pc from the source. FRB 240312D is therefore the first highly scattered FRB where scattering screens in the host galaxy centre, a background galaxy, or intervening structures can all be excluded, leaving only the circumsource medium. Integral field spectroscopy of the host reveals a Milky Way-like galaxy with a star-formation region at the FRB position. We find refractive scattering in a pulsar wind nebula as the most likely scattering origin. However, the explanation is not completely satisfactory as it requires a fine-tuned orientation. Hence, additional theoretical studies under different FRB progenitor models are needed. From the two FRBs, we calculate a total rate of Rₜot=210⁺⁴⁶⁰₋₁₈₀ events sky⁻¹day⁻¹ with durations between 55.2 ms and 1 s and above a fluence of 9 Jy ms consistent with the rate of shorter FRBs. This elevated rate suggests that the strong scattering seen in other FRBs likewise does not arise from chance-aligned sightlines but is instead linked to the FRB sources.

more.abstract: Traditional preimplantation genetic testing for in vitro fertilization (IVF) requires invasive trophectoderm biopsy, which may harm the embryo. Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) utilizing cell-free DNA from spent embryo culture medium (SCM) has been attempted, but trace DNA content, maternal cell contamination and high allele drop-out rates are barriers. Here we report an niPGT methodology achieving high diagnostic accuracy among reportable samples across diverse embryo and disease contexts. Reengineered linear whole-genome amplification (scm-LIANTI) with an extremely low error rate is followed by application of a Bayesian algorithm designed to determine which parental haplotypes are inherited at disease-causing sites. Among 191 SCM samples from 29 families affected by rare monogenic disorders, our method amplified all samples and enabled diagnosis of 220 out of 277 pathogenic alleles. All diagnoses (220/220) were concordant with invasive biopsy control. For select embryos, personalized genome-wide genotyping enabled exploratory polygenic risk assessment for type 2 diabetes. Our methodology requires no modification to IVF workflows and represents a key technological advance towards scalable, accurate and safe niPGT for both monogenic and polygenic diseases.

more.title: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes
more.abstract: Oxygen minimum zones, subsurface regions of the ocean severely depleted in dissolved oxygen, today extend over more than 30 million km 2. Although these areas are expected to expand in the future in response to warming, the magnitude of deoxygenation is poorly constrained. Here we present a quantitative spatio-temporal reconstruction of oxygen minimum zone changes in the subarctic and eastern North Pacific over the last 55 thousand years based on 2,569 individual foraminiferal assemblage measurements from 11 sedimentary cores. We find that the extent of oxygen minimum zones in the eastern North Pacific expanded in response to warming during Dansgaard–Oeschger events during the last glacial period and through the last deglaciation. However, re-oxygenation events and oxygen minimum zone contraction also occurred in the last glacial period when overturning circulation weakened in the North Atlantic during Heinrich events. Our findings, supported by Earth system simulations confirming a strong coupling between millennial-scale changes in North Atlantic circulation and North Pacific oxygen minimum zone extent, imply a complex future response of the oxygen minimum zone extent, with global circulation changes potentially mitigating the direct effects of warming.

more.abstract: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. more.abstract: We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations of the field of the fast X-ray transient (FXT) detected by Einstein Probe, EP250207b, to resolve any ambiguity about the host galaxy and redshift of the FXT. EP250207b was originally associated with a nearby galaxy at z = 0.082, based on its low chance alignment probability, and a binary neutron star merger origin was proposed. However, we report the detection of a background galaxy at z = 3.2 at the location of EP250207b. Assuming this galaxy is the actual host galaxy, the rest-frame energetics and timescales of the event change. Furthermore, the available data are not able to rule out the presence of a supernova associated with EP250207b if at this redshift. We model the X-ray, optical, near-infrared and radio light curves using a tophat jet model implemented in Redback and find that they are consistent with an on-axis gamma ray burst afterglow. The energetics and host galaxy properties do not allow us to distinguish between a collapsar and a merger driven event.

Corporate campaign spending is systematically associated with the likelihood that a ballot measure passes. shortlist.abstract: We give a deterministic O (m log 2/3 n)-time algorithm for single-source shortest paths (SSSP) on directed graphs with real non-negative edge weights in the comparison-addition model. This is the first result to break the O (m+n log n) time bound of Dijkstra’s algorithm on sparse graphs, showing that Dijkstra’s algorithm is not optimal for SSSP.

shortlist.title: Nonadiabatic theory of phonon magnetic moments in insulators and metals
shortlist.abstract: We develop a nonadiabatic theory of phonon magnetic moments applicable to both insulators and metals. By relating the phonon magnetic moment to the force-velocity response of ions in a magnetic field, we derive a gauge-invariant expression using a gauge-covariant Wigner expansion. The formalism naturally separates Fermi-sea and Fermi-surface contributions and captures the full dependence on phonon frequency. In gapped systems, our theory reduces to previous adiabatic expressions in the low-frequency limit. Beyond this limit, it reveals additional contributions arising from resonant interband processes and the Fermi surface. Applying our theory to Pb 1 − x Sn x Te, we find that the Fermi-surface contribution substantially enhances the phonon magnetic moment, reproducing the same order of magnitude as the experimental observation. Our results provide a unified framework for describing phonon magnetic moments beyond the adiabatic regime.

shortlist.title: Plasma waveguides for high-intensity laser pulses
shortlist.abstract: Fundamental to many applications of laser pulses in science and technology is an extended interaction length with matter that significantly exceeds the distance over which the pulse would normally diffract and transversely spread. At low intensity, the interaction could simply be the linear refraction provided by a glass optical fiber to keep the pulse from spreading. At higher pulse intensities, however, the goal extends beyond diffraction-free pulse transport: an extended interaction length of high intensity light can give rise to bright secondary sources of photons and, at relativistic intensities, beams of high energy charged particles. Since these applications require laser intensities well above the threshold for ionization of atoms, new methods for overcoming pulse diffraction in a plasma have been developed. Chief among them are plasma waveguides  optical fibers composed of plasma, with characteristic mode structure. This article reviews the methods and theory of plasma waveguides, highlighting the recent development of meter-scale plasma waveguides that have been instrumental to the laser acceleration of high-charge electron beams to energies ~10 GeV.

shortlist.title: Probing the Memory of a Superconducting Qubit Environment
shortlist.abstract: Achieving fault tolerance with superconducting quantum processors requires qubits to operate within the regime of threshold theorems based on the Born-Markov approximation. This approximation, which models dissipation as constant energy decay into a memoryless environment, breaks down when qubits couple to long-lived two-level systems (TLSs) that become polarized during operation and retain memory of past qubit states. Here, we show that non-Poissonian quantum jump traces carry the information required to distinguish long-lived TLSs from the standard Markovian bath. By fitting the Solomon equations to measured quantum jump dynamics arising naturally from thermal fluctuations, we can disentangle the qubit’s coupling to the two environments. Sweeping the qubit frequency reveals distinct peaks, each associated with a TLS that outlives the qubit, providing a handle to understand their microscopic origin.

shortlist.title: Separability of the motion of spinning test particles in curved space-time
shortlist.abstract: Solving for the motion of spinning test particles in curved spacetimes is important for modeling gravitational-wave inspirals of spinning compact binaries. We build a Hamiltonian formalism in worldline-adapted frames for the spinning test particle and formulate a corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi equation valid to linear order in spin. We prove that when the geodesic motion in a spacetime and the parallel transport along said geodesics are both separable, then so is the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The key insight is that the transform to the worldline-adapted frame that separates parallel transport also coincidentally generates a near-identity transform into separation coordinates in the orbital sector. We illustrate this in black hole, plane wave, and cosmological spacetimes.

shortlist.title: Optimal discrimination of Gaussian states by Gaussian measurements
shortlist.abstract: Are Gaussian measurements enough to distinguish between Gaussian states? Here, we tackle this question by focusing on the max-relative entropy as an operational distinguishability metric. Given two multimode Gaussian states ρ , σ with covariance matrices V σ > V ρ , we derive a condition that completely determines whether or not there exists an optimal Gaussian measurement achieving the max-relative entropy. When the condition is satisfied, we find this optimal measurement explicitly. When the condition is not met, there is a strict gap between the distinguishability achievable by Gaussian measurements and the unconstrained max-relative entropy in which all measurements are allowed. We illustrate our results in the single-mode setting, and show examples of states for which this gap can be made arbitrarily large, revealing novel instances of Gaussian data hiding.

shortlist.title: Mapping Dust Attenuation at Kiloparsec Scales. III. The 2175 Å Bump
shortlist.abstract: We combine the Swift/UVOT+MaNGA catalog with Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) K s imaging to map the 2175 Å attenuation bump at kiloparsec scales in nearby galaxies. We use two complementary estimators: an ultraviolet-to-near-infrared attenuation-curve method, yielding A bump UOIR and B for 2487 high-continuum-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) spaxels, and the near-ultraviolet-only method of A. Battisti et al., yielding A bump NUV and k bump for 7934 spaxels. The two absolute bump estimates agree well where they overlap. We compare bump strength with local stellar-population, emission-line, attenuation-curve, and geometric diagnostics after separating star-forming (SF) and non-SF regions. The strongest bumps occur at low specific H α surface brightness, Σ H α /Σ *, especially in non-SF regions, where this ratio traces ionized-gas emission per unit stellar mass rather than sSFR. The bump also weakens with EW(H α) and strengthens with D n 4000 and stellar age. In contrast, metallicity, inclination, galactocentric radius, A V, and optical attenuation-curve slope are secondary predictors. The absolute strength A bump NUV increases with Σ H α and Σ *, while the relative strengths k bump and B do not, indicating that absolute bump amplitude partly follows dust column whereas normalized strengths better trace effective bump prominence. These results support local radiation-field processing of the 2175 Å carriers.

shortlist.title: A Warped Dust Ring in the CQ Tau Disk
shortlist.abstract: The diversity of planetary orbital architectures calls for observational constraints on radial variations in disk-plane orientation, or warps, yet such variations in dust disks remain poorly characterized. CQ Tau is a promising target because its misaligned inner disk and candidate gas warp suggest a radially extended warp. We present the ALMA 1.3 mm dust continuum image reconstructed from the real part of the visibilities, extracting the centro-symmetric disk structure. At an effective spatial resolution of 0. ″ 052 × 0. ″ 042 (7.8 × 6.3 au), the image reveals a bright main ring at radii of ∼20–70 au and an unresolved compact emission component tracing the inner disk around the central star. Ellipse fits centered on the stellar position to contours tracing the inner and outer edges of the ring reveal radial variations in position angles and inclinations. At the inner edge (∼21–26 au), the position angle and inclination span 214 ∘ –233 ∘ and 23 ∘ –39 ∘, respectively, while they span 231 ∘ –235 ∘ and 33 ∘ –36 ∘ at the outer edge (∼58–67 au). Whereas a coplanar ring toy model fails to reproduce such variations, a warped ring model with the local tilt decreasing from ∼4 ∘ at r = 20 au to ∼1 ∘ at 60 au reproduces them. The high-pass-filtered real-part image reveals a pair of opposed curved negative residuals. Similar features appear only in the warped ring model, further supporting the dust warp. These results establish CQ Tau as an example of a warped dust disk and an important laboratory for investigating the connection between three-dimensional disk geometry and planet formation.

shortlist.title: STIR: Reed–Solomon Proximity Testing with Fewer Queries
shortlist.abstract: We present STIR (Shift To Improve Rate), an interactive oracle proof of proximity (IOPP) for Reed–Solomon codes that achieves the best known query complexity of any concretely efficient IOPP for this problem. For λ bits of security, STIR has query complexity O (log d + λ ⋅ loglog d), while FRI, a popular protocol, has query complexity O (λ ⋅ log d) (including variants of FRI based on conjectured security assumptions). STIR relies on a new technique for recursively improving the rate of the tested Reed–Solomon code. We provide an implementation of STIR compiled to a SNARK. Compared to a highly-optimized implementation of FRI, STIR achieves an improvement in argument size that ranges from 1.25× to 2.46× depending on the chosen parameters, with similar prover and verifier running times. For example, in order to achieve 128 bits of security for degree 2 26 and rate 1/4, STIR has argument size 114 KiB, compared to 211 KiB for FRI.

shortlist.title: Nanoscale Flexibility Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative Water Sorption
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Passive, sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting technologies (AWHTs) have attracted recent interest as an alternative to energy-intensive condensation-based technologies. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer wide chemical tunability to design sorbents, but in practice, sorbents must retain moisture during humidity fluctuations, and small adsorption enthalpies are necessary for regeneration of the sorbent material. Here, we report that Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles with diameters less than 120 nm exhibit structural flexibility at the Cu2+ centers that enables a “breathing”-type cooperative water sorption. This cooperative structural phase change occurs only for nanoparticles that contain Cu2+, and not for the isomorphic magnesium triazolate. The phase change significantly decreases the onset pressures of adsorption and desorption compared to large particles and opens a practically useful hysteresis window in the isotherms, while maintaining small adsorption enthalpies (48 kJ/mol averaged over the isotherm, approaching the 44 kJ/mol latent heat of water at low RH). Mechanistic analysis indicates that adsorption initiates with weak electrostatic and dispersion interactions between water and triazolate rings brought into close proximity only by the distorted Cu2+ centers of the nanoparticles. Together, these results present a distinct water sorption mechanism and design strategy that leverages size- and metal-dependent lattice flexibility in a wide class of porous materials.

shortlist.title: Resolving Chlorine Sites in Pharmaceuticals by Integrated Site-Resolved Zeeman-Perturbed NQR, Solid-State NMR, and Electron Diffraction Crystallography
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and high-value chemicals feature covalently bonded chlorine functionalities that influence molecular packing, stability, and bioavailability. However, site-resolved structural characterization of chlorine sites in powders remains challenging, especially in systems with multiple chemically or crystallographically nonequivalent sites, disorder, or hydration sensitivity. We report here a novel combined 35Cl nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR), 35Cl Zeeman-perturbed NQR (Zp-NQR), 35Cl solid-state NMR, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED/microcrystal electron diffraction) approach to characterizing powdered chlorine-bearing chemicals. Case studies of ketoconazole and chloramine-T demonstrate the utility of the approach in characterizing local structural heterogeneity and the hydration state. The role of crystal packing and noncovalent interactions on the spectroscopic observables is provided through an analysis of chlorzoxazone and five of its cocrystals, of which three are novel. Compared to ultrahigh-field NMR spectra alone, NQR and Zp-NQR spectra provide improved sensitivity to small changes in the electric field gradient and in the degree of disorder around chlorine. Experimental NQR/Zp-NQR data combined with gauge-including projector augmented-wave density functional theory (GIPAW-DFT) provide local structural constraints for a partially dehydrated chloramine-T phase. The refinement protocol does not require single crystals, and in the case of NQR experiments, intact tablets containing APIs are analyzed directly without further treatment or grinding. As a proof of principle, commercial tablets are shown to contain ketoconazole in the same crystalline form as that seen for the pure API. The general approach…

shortlist.title: Whistler Wave Generation from Lower-hybrid Turbulence in Solar Flares: Implications for Radio Fiber Bursts
shortlist.abstract: We report the identification of whistler wave generation by ion-ring-driven lower-hybrid (LH) turbulence in solar flare plasma environments using fully kinetic two-dimensional (2D) particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. While previous studies established that ion rings excite LH waves capable of accelerating electrons to hard X-ray (HXR) energies, the generation of secondary whistler waves—required to explain radio fiber bursts—remains unresolved. We contrast two regimes at a fixed ring velocity v r: a sub-Alfvénic (v r < V A) case (δ = ω pe /Ω ce = 0.5) and a super-Alfvénic (v r > V A) case (δ = 5.0). In the sub-Alfvénic case, the ring-driven instability is initially electrostatic. LH waves reach large amplitudes and accelerate electrons to 20–100 keV, capable of producing HXR emission. Crucially, whistler waves subsequently emerge via nonlinear wave–particle scattering. Conversely, in the super-Alfvénic case, the system is forced into an electromagnetic regime. Here, whistlers are directly and linearly excited—evidenced by the simultaneous exponential growth of electric and magnetic fluctuations. However, electron Landau damping restricts the wave spectrum to a limited range of small parallel wavenumbers, reducing parallel electron acceleration (≲10 keV). By capturing the kinetic transition from the sub- to the super-Alfvénic regime, these idealized limits suggest a microscopic framework for the established model of solar flares: ion-ring drivers could self-consistently power both HXR-producing electrons in dense footpoints and the whistler populations required for radio fiber bursts in weaker-field coronal exhausts.

shortlist.title: The Contribution of Starspots to the Lithium Spread in NGC 2264
shortlist.abstract: Star clusters with ages of a few Myr have a previously unexplained dispersion in the lithium equivalent widths. In this work, we show that much of the lithium spread of the young cluster NGC 2264 can be attributed to the observational presence of starspots. We demonstrate that the equivalent width of Li i 6708 Å changes with observed spot coverage, using a sample of 15 Weak-Lined T Tauri Stars (WTTSs) with multiepoch high-resolution ESPaDOnS spectra and photometry. To quantify the contribution of starspots, we construct an empirical two-component starspot model. When differences in visible spot coverage are taken into account, 68% of the WTTSs fall within the model-predicted EW(Li) dispersion for a range from 0% to 90% visible spot coverage. We find no correlation between the age spread or gravity and Li i equivalent width in NGC 2264. Our results suggest that invoking starspots can explain much of the apparent lithium spread in NGC 2264 and reduces but does not fully eliminate the need to invoke rotation-driven lithium depletion or other nonstandard explanations at such young ages. Future simultaneous measurements of lithium and beryllium in young stars may provide an independent test of this scenario.

shortlist.title: G:C:G:C-Flanked i-Motifs Are Thermodynamically Favored and Their Sequences Highly Enriched in the Human Genome
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: i-Motifs are biologically relevant noncanonical DNA structures whose stability is strongly influenced by capping interactions. Among these, minor groove tetrads (MGTs) are among the most powerful stabilizing elements identified to date, yet the molecular factors governing their effects and their potential biological significance remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic experimental and computational analysis of 16 MGT-stabilized i-motifs (MGTiMs), encompassing all combinations of terminal tetrad composition and orientation within a common sequence scaffold. NMR spectroscopy confirms that all sequences adopt closely related architectures, enabling direct comparison of the effects of tetrad identity and orientation on stability. Thermal denaturation experiments reveal that the stability hierarchy, previously observed in selected structures (G:C:G:C ≳ G:C:G:T ≫ G:T:G:T), is broadly maintained across the series, although substantial positional effects are observed. Molecular dynamics simulations and energy decomposition analyses suggest that differences in electrostatic interactions and local conformational flexibility contribute to these trends. Notably, genome-wide analysis of the human genome reveals a strong enrichment of sequences capable of forming the most stabilizing tetrads, with motifs containing two G:C:G:C tetrads reaching a 45-fold enrichment relative to random expectation. Interestingly, this most abundant genomic motif is also the only one that undergoes pronounced pH-driven conformational transitions, highlighting the unique structural plasticity of these architectures. Together, these findings reveal how tetrad composition and positional context govern MGTiM stability and identify NN-type motifs as a particularly enriched class of…

shortlist.title: Extremal Fitting Problems for Conjunctive Queries
shortlist.abstract: The fitting problem for conjunctive queries (CQs) is the problem to construct a CQ that fits a given set of labeled data examples. When a fitting CQ exists, it is in general not unique. This leads us to propose natural refinements of the notion of a fitting CQ, such as most-general fitting CQ, most-specific fitting CQ, and unique fitting CQ. We give structural characterizations of these notions in terms of (suitable refinements of) homomorphism dualities, frontiers, and direct products, which enable the construction of the refined fitting CQs when they exist. We also pinpoint the complexity of the associated existence and verification problems, and determine the size of fitting CQs. We study the same problems for unions of CQs (UCQs).

shortlist.title: A Unique Conformationally Assisted [2+2] Configuration in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Two π-conjugated macrocycles, namely the well-known [12]cycloparaphenylene and a newly designed macrocycle combining benzenes and rigid stilbene units, are presented for the first time as light-amplifying gain media in distributed feedback (DFB) laser devices. Both systems show good photonic functionality arising from a four-state photonic cycle comprising a [2+2] state configuration (two delocalized and two conformationally distorted localized states). The mechanism involves the generation of two optically coupled states through excited-state structural distortion induced during internal conversion, which reduces light reabsorption losses and promotes rapid population inversion. Comprehensive steady-state absorption and fluorescence and transient absorption spectroscopy studies are conducted in order to reveal the nature of the low energy lying excited states. Furthermore, amplified spontaneous emission studies of the compounds in polystyrene thin films, followed by the preparation and characterization of optically pumped DFB lasers, were performed. The results reveal new properties of these multifunctional cyclic π-conjugated molecules and unique structure-property relationships.
