shortlist.title: The Complexity of Subgame-perfect Equilibria in Parity and Mean-payoff Games
shortlist.abstract: In this article, we prove that the SPE constrained existence problem, i.e., the problem of deciding, in a given game, the existence of a subgame-perfect equilibrium that generates a payoff profile between two given thresholds, is NP-complete for both parity games and mean-payoff games. For that purpose, we use the notion of negotiation function, and the fact that a play is compatible with an SPE if and only if it is consistent with a fixed point of that function. Our algorithms consist in guessing (1) such a fixed point, (2) a certificate of the existence of a play consistent with that fixed point that matches the constraints, and (3) a certificate proving that it is a fixed point.

shortlist.title: Screening for Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
shortlist.abstract: Background: Previous reviews on prostate cancer screening relied on ongoing trials of invitations to screening with prostate-specific antigen (PSA), which may lack sufficient follow-up for mortality and overdiagnosis. Other screening tests with higher specificity may improve the benefit–harm profile. Purpose: To examine benefits and harms of screening versus no screening or usual care. Data Sources: MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (2014 to 28 January 2026); reviews and included studies for studies published before 2014. Study Selection: Paired reviewers identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective nonrandomized studies. Benefit outcomes relied on data reported by age when possible. Data Extraction: Paired reviewers extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted with investigation of heterogeneity; assessment of certainty of evidence used the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach with decision thresholds as the targets of certainty. Data Synthesis: Thirteen RCTs ( n = 792 034; 8 from a multisite European trial, and 1 for harms only) and 3 uncontrolled cohort studies ( n = 5593; all for harms) were included. All RCTs compared invitations to PSA-based screening versus no invitation. At 20 years’ follow-up, among 1000 men who were invited to multiple rounds of PSA-based screening every 2 to 4 years starting at age 55 to 69 years (mean, 62 years), there was likely a reduction in prostate cancer mortality (≥2 fewer) and metastatic cancer incidence (≥6 fewer) at the expense of prostate cancer overdiagnosis (≥20 cases) and false positives (≥150 cases) (all moderate certainty). Advancements based on performance parameters like extraction efficiency, selectivity, solvent recovery, toxicity, and scalability for major families of GSs along with discussions of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing solvent-biomolecule interactions, solvent polarity, hydrogen-bonding, viscosity, mass transfer, and solvent nanostructure are critically evaluated. Because favourable solvent properties do not by themselves ensure a greener process, particular attention is given to comparisons with conventional solvents, preservation of biomolecule quality, downstream product recovery and solvent regeneration, and representative techno-economic and life-cycle case studies, with greenness assessed at the process level rather than inferred from solvent origin. Furthermore, the integration of GSs with advanced extraction technologies, including ultrasound, microwave, and pressurised liquid-assisted extraction, is discussed, with particular emphasis placed on synergistic strategies that enhance extraction performance while reducing energy and solvent consumption. Finally, GS-based spin-offs, regulatory considerations, and key challenges including predictive solvent selection, process scale-up, and digital solvent discovery are critically assessed. Emerging opportunities offered by hybrid GS systems, machine learning-guided solvent design, integrated biorefineries, and omics-enabled extraction are also highlighted. shortlist.title: Movies’ Content Features Predict the Personalities of Their Fans
shortlist.abstract: Movies are a central form of entertainment and cultural expression, yet little is known about how their content aligns with the psychological traits of their audiences. We link movie characteristics and contents with the aggregate Big Five personalities of social-media users from a large, international sample who “liked” them. Movie content, captured by text keywords, predicts aggregate audience personalities beyond genre, demographics, and attributes like quality and popularity. An online experiment (N = 1,018 adults) demonstrates that these content-based personality predictions are behaviorally relevant for choices and evaluations involving new movies and participants. We further provide fine-grained mappings between personality and movie features, including quality, popularity, genre, psychological themes, and unique concepts. Our findings reveal systematic links between personality and movie preferences, showing that people favor content that resonates with their thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. This research enables scalable, automated audience psychographic assessment based on content features, offering insights into personality-driven media preferences.

shortlist.title: The potential of nanosized zeolites in catalysis
shortlist.abstract: Zeolites with well-defined microporous frameworks are among the most widely utilized heterogeneous catalysts in petroleum refining, fine chemical synthesis, and environmental protection. However, the intrinsic diffusion limitations associated with conventional micron-sized crystals often restrict catalytic efficiency, product selectivity, and catalyst lifetime, particularly in reactions involving bulky molecules. Reducing zeolite crystal dimensions to the nanoscale has emerged as an effective strategy to alleviate transport constraints, increase external surface area, and tailor the distribution and accessibility of acid sites. As a result, nanosized zeolites have attracted significant attention as advanced catalytic materials with enhanced activity, selectivity, and stability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in nanosized zeolites, with particular emphasis on the relationship between crystal size, diffusion phenomena, acidity, and catalytic performance. The discussion is organized according to the most industrially relevant framework topologies, including 12-membered-ring zeolites (FAU, *BEA, MOR, and LTL), 10-membered-ring zeolites (MFI, FER, MWW, and MEL), and the 8-membered-ring zeolite (CHA). Each topology is critically analyzed individually, while comparative summaries are provided to highlight key structural and catalytic trends. Diverse nanoscale architectures including aggregated and monodispersed nanoparticles, self-pillared and intergrown structures, intra-crystalline mesoporous systems, finned morphologies, and nanosheets are examined to illustrate how structural design governs diffusion pathways and catalytic behavior. Particular attention is devoted to the incorporation of heteroatoms and the modulation of acidity, which…

shortlist.title: Nanotechnology Meets Brain Diseases: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies for Drug Delivery
shortlist.abstract: Brain diseases, encompassing neurodegenerative disorders, cerebrovascular diseases, and brain tumors, impose a profound global health burden. Conventional therapeutic strategies often fail due to the formidable blood–brain barrier (BBB) and complex pathological microenvironment of the central nervous system (CNS). The rapid evolution of nanotechnology offers unprecedented opportunities to overcome these delivery hurdles. This review comprehensively summarizes recent developments in engineered nanoplatforms for the diagnosis and targeted therapy of brain diseases. It first outlines the pathological characteristics and nanoprobe-enhanced diagnostic methods for various brain disorders, followed by a critical evaluation of five major classes of nanocarriers for CNS drug delivery: lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, bio-derived, and hybrid nanocarriers. This evaluation highlights their structural attributes and delivery efficiencies. The discussion then examines advanced strategies to improve delivery precision, including multilevel targeting (e.g., BBB penetration and specific cell targeting), stimuli-responsive theranostics, and functional surface modifications. Linking these nanotechnological innovations to specific neurological diseases highlights their clinical potential. Finally, the review addresses current translational challenges, including biosafety, scalable manufacturing, and interindividual variability, and offers a forward-looking perspective on the rational design of next-generation precision neuro-nanomedicines.

shortlist.title: Generative AI And Creative Goods: Market Expansion, Crowd-Out, and Copyright
shortlist.abstract: We study how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) affects creative goods markets using data from a large stock images marketplace. In December 2022, the platform announced it would allow artists to sell GenAI-produced images, subject to two conditions: all GenAI images must be labeled, and GenAI would be prohibited in certain markets. We exploit this policy variation using a difference-in-differences design. We estimate a 136% increase in image production and 47% increase in active artists, accompanied by a 15% decline in non-GenAI production and 29% decline in non-GenAI active artists. On the demand side, total sales increase by 82%, but non-GenAI sales fall by 28% and non-GenAI sales rates decline by 3 percentage points. We use image embeddings to develop novel measures of image quality, characteristics, and market composition.We find that quality (measured as predicted sales probability) increases by 9 percentage points overall and 2 percentage points for non-GenAI content, suggesting low-quality non-GenAI artists exit. Our product characteristic measures indicate that GenAI production is heavily concentrated in characteristic space, potentially limiting the value of these images to the market. Non-GenAI production responds to GenAI by differentiating into niches. We discuss implications for copyright policy and the longer-run sustainability of original creative work.

shortlist.title: Layered superlattices: from physical assembly to chemical synthesis and emerging applications
shortlist.abstract: Quantum materials offer a powerful platform for exploring emergent condensed matter phenomena and developing functional devices, owing to their tunable electronic structures, quasiparticle excitations and collective quantum effects. Layered superlattices are a class of layered heterostructures formed by the periodic stacking of two or more sublattices along the direction perpendicular to the layers, with the constituent layers differing in composition, structure, or electronic properties. Such structural versatility establishes layered superlattices as a materials platform for connecting emergent quantum states with functional implementation. This review systematically summarizes the classification of sublattices in layered superlattices, including systems composed of inorganic sublattices and hybrid architectures comprising organic components and coordination-complex building blocks. It then discusses the major fabrication strategies, ranging from physical assembly to chemical synthesis, with an emphasis on the material compatibility, structural controllability and scalability of each approach. The review examines how quantum confinement, resonant tunneling, interlayer coupling and cooperative interfacial effects govern emergent physical properties and device performance. Recent progress in superconductivity, thermoelectrics, optoelectronic detection, sensing, and energy storage and conversion is also summarized. Finally, this review discusses key challenges in structural control, scalable synthesis, stability improvement, dynamic characterization and nonequilibrium photophysics, while highlighting future opportunities enabled by machine learning, high-throughput experimentation, multiscale simulations and advanced characterization. shortlist.abstract: The thermal' fluctuation spectrum of the electric field arising due to particle noise in a quiescent Vlasov--Poisson plasma was derived in the 1960s. Here, we derive the universal fluctuation spectrum of the electric field, at Debye and sub-Debye scales, for a turbulent Vlasov--Poisson plasma. This spectrum arises from what is likely to be the final cascade’—a universal regime to be encountered at the extreme small-scale end of any turbulent cascade in a nearly collisionless plasma. The cascaded invariant is the generalized (negative) entropy C 2 , which is the quadratic Casimir invariant of the particle distribution function. C 2 cascades to small scales in both position and velocity space via both linear and nonlinear phase mixing, in such a way that the timescales associated with the two processes are `critically balanced’ at every scale. We construct a phenomenological scaling theory of the fluctuation spectrum of C 2 in ( k , s ) space—and hence of the electric field in k space—in arbitrary dimensions, where k and s are the spatial and velocity wavenumbers, respectively. The electric-field spectrum is sufficiently steep for the nonlinear mixing to be controlled by the largest-scale electric fluctuations, and so the C 2 cascade resembles the Batchelor cascade of a passive scalar, albeit in the kinetic phase space. The conclusions of our theory are corroborated by direct numerical simulations of a forced 1D-1V plasma. We predict that the cascade is ultimately terminated at the (spatial) wavenumber where the turbulent electric-field spectrum gives way to the fluctuation spectrum associated with discrete particle noise; this transition scale is set by the amplitude of the turbulent electric fields and the plasma parameter. shortlist.abstract: We undertake a global analysis of institutional investor portfolios and find widespread underweighting of companies with higher carbon emissions, both in levels and intensities. This underweighting is largely driven by foreign companies with high carbon emissions, both at the intensive (tilting) and extensive (exclusion) margins. Domestic firms with high emissions are overweighted but by a smaller magnitude. These results reveal a bias for domestic companies with high carbon emissions. The carbon home bias is stronger in settings where institutions have tighter business connections, in countries with weaker social norms regarding climate crisis, and where the political environment is more polarized.

For the first time, we extract double distributions (DDs) directly from lattice data, therefore enforcing an important property of GPDs linked to Lorentz symmetry. We use the flexible framework of multidimensional Gaussian process regression to regularize the inverse problem and present an assessment of the impact of model dependence on the systematic uncertainty. Our lattice ensemble corresponds to a pion mass m π = 358 MeV and a lattice spacing a = 0.094 fm. We use larger hadron momenta, up to 2.7 GeV, and kinematic coverage compared to our previous computations, and extract additional skewness-dependent moments of the GPD.

shortlist.abstract: Measures of overconfidence are used both to assess biases in people’s beliefs regarding their own abilities and to identify correlates of those biases. Proposed correlates of overconfidence include narcissism, social status, (low) task anxiety, savings, planning, and many more. Research on these correlates typically explicitly or implicitly claims that the associations with overconfidence are not attributable to ability (i.e., latent inputs enabling successful task performance, including inputs that vary across people, states, or contexts). I argue that several typical approaches used to measure overconfidence are not sufficient to support such claims. This argument follows from two underappreciated properties of these measures of overconfidence. First, performance is an imperfect measure of ability: accounting for performance does not sufficiently account for ability. Second, self-evaluations of performance should reflect ability in addition to performance: because performance is ambiguous, people should incorporate prior beliefs about their ability. These properties imply that multiple commonly used measures of overconfidence are confounded with ability. I support these analytical results by reexamining previously published findings. In the first analysis, I find that overconfidence predicts subsequent performance, consistent with measures of overconfidence serving as a signal of ability. In the second set of analyses, I find that some purported associations between overconfidence and other constructs could be attributed to ability instead. shortlist.title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates
shortlist.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
shortlist.abstract: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client-scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client-scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client-scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue-resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach for partitioning can be extended to other biomolecules, offering a framework to analyze their partitioning in cellular environments.

shortlist.title: Determinants of Norm Compliance: Moral Similarity and Group Identification
shortlist.abstract: What determines whether someone complies with a social norm? The social identity approach offers a mechanism for norm compliance: A person who feels similar to a group identifies more with that group and, in turn, complies with the group’s norms. Using an experiment, we test whether similarity in values increases identification and adherence to a group rule. To do so, we varied the similarity/dissimilarity between the values of an individual and members of a social group and measured group identification and rule compliance. We find that moral similarity in progressivism increases group identification, and group identification can increase compliance with rules from the social group. However, our results also suggest that this relationship can be disrupted. Because of our design and empirically verified in our study, social norms do not differ between treatments. As a consequence, observed behavior changes are attributable to increased group norm sensitivity and not changes in group norms. We advance the study of social identity by testing a causal pathway between group identification, group norm sensitivity, and behavior change. Our contribution to the management literature is to extend the empirical rationale, and cautionary notes, for investing in value-alignment between individuals and organizations. shortlist.title: Spectroscopic Evidence of Competing Diagonal Spin Interactions and Spin Disproportionation in the Bilayer Nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7
shortlist.abstract: A comprehensive spectroscopic map of the electronic, magnetic, and lattice excitations is presented for the bilayer nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7 using Raman scattering at ambient pressure. Upon entering the spin density wave state below 153 K, the A 1 g channel exhibits an abrupt electronic spectral gap with a clear isosbestic point. In contrast, the B 1 g and B 2 g channels are dominated by pronounced two-magnon (2M) excitations, representing a signature of incipient Mottness. These 2M signals in both channels constitute evidence for two distinct in-plane spin-exchange interactions along the Ni—O bonding and its diagonal directions. Calculations based on the spin wave theory further reveal that the 2M mode in the B 2 g channel arises from the competition between two bond-diagonal antiferromagnetic interactions mediated by nickel d x 2 − y 2 orbitals. Furthermore, emergent low-energy 2M excitations below 10 meV are found to originate from distinct, weaker spin moments, supporting spin disproportionation. Simultaneously, an anomalous softening of B 1 g phonons from 280 down to 4.5 K is uncovered, suggesting the presence of an incipient lattice instability leading to checkerboard-type breathing modulations. Collectively, these findings identify a ground state of the bilayer nickelate characterized by competing bond-diagonal interactions, spin disproportionation, and an incipient lattice instability, establishing key ingredients for understanding the mechanism of nickelate superconductivity.

shortlist.title: Two new highly scattered fast radio bursts: evidence for scatter broadening by the circumsource medium
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We found two highly scattered Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) during commissioning of the Commensal Realtime ASKAP Fast Transient COherent (CRACO) backend. FRB 240210D and FRB 240312D have scattering times of 34 ± 6 and 300 ± 48 ms, respectively, when scaled to 1 GHz. FRB 240312D originates near a spiral arm of a face-on galaxy at a redshift of only 0.05. Scintillation from a Milky Way screen constrains the distance of the scattering screen to ∼10 pc from the source. FRB 240312D is therefore the first highly scattered FRB where scattering screens in the host galaxy centre, a background galaxy, or intervening structures can all be excluded, leaving only the circumsource medium. Integral field spectroscopy of the host reveals a Milky Way-like galaxy with a star-formation region at the FRB position. We find refractive scattering in a pulsar wind nebula as the most likely scattering origin. However, the explanation is not completely satisfactory as it requires a fine-tuned orientation. Hence, additional theoretical studies under different FRB progenitor models are needed. From the two FRBs, we calculate a total rate of Rₜot=210⁺⁴⁶⁰₋₁₈₀ events sky⁻¹day⁻¹ with durations between 55.2 ms and 1 s and above a fluence of 9 Jy ms consistent with the rate of shorter FRBs. This elevated rate suggests that the strong scattering seen in other FRBs likewise does not arise from chance-aligned sightlines but is instead linked to the FRB sources.

shortlist.title: Highly accurate non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic and polygenic diseases from spent medium
shortlist.abstract: Traditional preimplantation genetic testing for in vitro fertilization (IVF) requires invasive trophectoderm biopsy, which may harm the embryo. Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) utilizing cell-free DNA from spent embryo culture medium (SCM) has been attempted, but trace DNA content, maternal cell contamination and high allele drop-out rates are barriers. Here we report an niPGT methodology achieving high diagnostic accuracy among reportable samples across diverse embryo and disease contexts. Reengineered linear whole-genome amplification (scm-LIANTI) with an extremely low error rate is followed by application of a Bayesian algorithm designed to determine which parental haplotypes are inherited at disease-causing sites. Among 191 SCM samples from 29 families affected by rare monogenic disorders, our method amplified all samples and enabled diagnosis of 220 out of 277 pathogenic alleles. All diagnoses (220/220) were concordant with invasive biopsy control. For select embryos, personalized genome-wide genotyping enabled exploratory polygenic risk assessment for type 2 diabetes. Our methodology requires no modification to IVF workflows and represents a key technological advance towards scalable, accurate and safe niPGT for both monogenic and polygenic diseases.

shortlist.title: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes
shortlist.abstract: Oxygen minimum zones, subsurface regions of the ocean severely depleted in dissolved oxygen, today extend over more than 30 million km 2. Although these areas are expected to expand in the future in response to warming, the magnitude of deoxygenation is poorly constrained. Here we present a quantitative spatio-temporal reconstruction of oxygen minimum zone changes in the subarctic and eastern North Pacific over the last 55 thousand years based on 2,569 individual foraminiferal assemblage measurements from 11 sedimentary cores. We find that the extent of oxygen minimum zones in the eastern North Pacific expanded in response to warming during Dansgaard–Oeschger events during the last glacial period and through the last deglaciation. However, re-oxygenation events and oxygen minimum zone contraction also occurred in the last glacial period when overturning circulation weakened in the North Atlantic during Heinrich events. Our findings, supported by Earth system simulations confirming a strong coupling between millennial-scale changes in North Atlantic circulation and North Pacific oxygen minimum zone extent, imply a complex future response of the oxygen minimum zone extent, with global circulation changes potentially mitigating the direct effects of warming.

shortlist.abstract: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. These visits generate negligible private investment value for the visiting funds. However, the information environment at the stock level improves following these visits with lower consensus analyst forecast errors. In addition to the information production role of these visits, they also generate positive externalities for other stakeholders through incremental improvements in the sustainability practices of the firms receiving sustainability-focused site visits from UNPRI fund managers. shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations of the field of the fast X-ray transient (FXT) detected by Einstein Probe, EP250207b, to resolve any ambiguity about the host galaxy and redshift of the FXT. EP250207b was originally associated with a nearby galaxy at z = 0.082, based on its low chance alignment probability, and a binary neutron star merger origin was proposed. However, we report the detection of a background galaxy at z = 3.2 at the location of EP250207b. Assuming this galaxy is the actual host galaxy, the rest-frame energetics and timescales of the event change. Furthermore, the available data are not able to rule out the presence of a supernova associated with EP250207b if at this redshift. We model the X-ray, optical, near-infrared and radio light curves using a tophat jet model implemented in Redback and find that they are consistent with an on-axis gamma ray burst afterglow. The energetics and host galaxy properties do not allow us to distinguish between a collapsar and a merger driven event.

shortlist.title: Corporate Contributions to Ballot Measure Campaigns: Real Effects and Valuation
shortlist.abstract: We analyze novel data on corporate contributions to ballot initiatives at the U.S. state level. Firms make large contributions to ballot measure campaigns in favor of or against specific initiatives. They contribute significantly more to business initiatives compared with ideological initiatives. Corporate campaign spending is systematically associated with the likelihood that a ballot measure passes. Contributing firms experience changes in sales growth following the passage of important ballot measures. Following successful (failed) initiatives, all firms in affected industries exhibit significantly more positive (negative) cumulative abnormal returns around the election, but contributing firms do more so than peers. shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Observations of local Seyfert galaxies show an intriguing connection between AGN luminosity and a deficit of molecular gas on ∼50 pc scales compared to 200 pc, the plausible imprint of AGN feedback. Motivated by these findings, we investigate the interplay between supermassive black hole (BH) accretion, AGN feedback, and nuclear gas reservoirs using cosmological hydrodynamic simulations implementing FIRE-3 multi-phase interstellar medium (ISM) physics and multi-component BH accretion and feedback models. Focusing on the late-time evolution of four Milky Way-mass galaxies, we find recurrent cycles of increased gas inflow toward the accretion disc, enhanced BH accretion, feedback self-regulation, and suppressed gas inflow rate until the next fuelling event. AGN winds interact with the ISM and escape preferentially through low-density polar channels after opening central cavities on ∼10–500 pc scales, regulating BH growth and producing episodic behaviour on ∼10–100 Myr timescales. The simulations reproduce the observed diversity of nuclear morphologies, gas concentrations, and AGN luminosities in late-type Seyfert galaxies, but do not exhibit a clear anti-correlation between gas concentration and AGN luminosity. Higher-luminosity AGN (LX ∼ 1041.5 − 43 erg s−1) powered by the accretion disc reservoir can coexist with feedback-driven cavities, consistent with observations, but they are more common in simulated galaxies with centrally-peaked gas distributions. Although differences in sample selection, tracer choice, spatial resolution, and stochasticity in AGN fuelling may impact underlying concentration-luminosity trends, the apparent tension between simulations and observations points to the timing between gas inflow, accretion-disc depletion, and feedback-driven clearing…

shortlist.title: Diverse lung challenges elicit a conserved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation blueprint
shortlist.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b + mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

shortlist.title: Conserved T cell receptor usage underpins recognition of CD1c presenting a mycobacterial lipid
shortlist.abstract: The mechanism by which αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) recognize mycobacterial lipids presented by CD1 family members is not well understood. We used CD1c tetramers loaded with the mycobacterial phosphomycoketide (PM) or mannosyl-PM to isolate T cells from healthy blood donors and individuals from a tuberculosis (TB)-endemic region of South Africa, with higher frequencies observed in individuals from the TB-endemic region. High-throughput analysis of >200 paired CD1c–mycoketide tetramer+ αβTCRs identified a conserved TCR motif, encoded by TRBV4-1 or TRBV7-9 variable region genes in greater than half of TCRs sequenced. A cryo-EM structure of a TRBV7-9+ TCR in complex with CD1c-PM demonstrated that the TCR bound to the A′-side of CD1c, directly contacting the phospholipid antigen and F′-portal residues. Analysis of multiple T cell clones interacting with CD1c mutants suggested that this TCR docking mode is representative of the larger TRBV7-9+ T cell population. Collectively, this study provides insight into mycobacterial lipid antigen recognition by αβ T cells restricted to CD1c.

shortlist.title: Aspiring to a Better Future: Can a Simple Psychological Intervention Reduce Poverty?
shortlist.abstract: Do higher aspirations for the future motivate people living in poverty to make long-term investments? Do their aspirations increase when economic conditions improve? To answer these questions, we run a 415-village field experiment with 8,300 women living in poverty in rural Kenya. We design an 80-minute workshop to help people set higher aspirations and plan to achieve them. We cross-randomise this with large unconditional cash transfers. The workshop substantially raises aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue, and living standards 17 months later, relative to a placebo workshop. Increases in aspirations are the most likely mechanism to explain the economic effects. Cash transfers also raise aspirations, which might help to explain why transfers increase labour supply and investment. We conclude that aspirations respond to both economic and psychological interventions, contribute to investment decisions and living standards, and are important considerations for development policy.

shortlist.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

shortlist.title: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias. Observations: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading. METHODS: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure–volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography). RESULTS: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34–67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0–65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0–42.0] mm Hg; P <0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P <0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183–242] to 160 [IQR, 129–204] mL; P <0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6–56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2–44.4] g; P <0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P =0.002). shortlist.title: Not Learning from Others
shortlist.abstract: We study social learning using experiments where two people independently learn relevant information and can share it to make accurate private decisions. Across three experiments, people are substantially less sensitive to information others discover than to equally-relevant information they discovered themselves. This holds when they must learn information from others through discussion; when the experimenter perfectly communicates the information; and even when participants observe others’ information with their own eyes. Our results therefore stem not from a failure to elicit information from others but a systematic tendency to underweight it relative to one’s own information. Our findings illustrate a powerful barrier to social learning that might underlie many documented cases of failure to learn from others.

Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
shortlist.abstract: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. The combination of a sensor suite, estimators, and a low-level controller achieved centimeter-scale positional flight accuracy. In addition, we developed a hierarchical controller in which a human operator provides high-level commands to direct the robot's motion. In a 30-second flight experiment conducted outside a motion-capture system, the robot avoided obstacles and ultimately landed on a sunflower. This level of sensing and computational autonomy represents a notable advancement for the aerial microrobotics community, opening further opportunities to explore onboard planning and power autonomy.

CAR-T Targeting of Mutant Calreticulin Selectively Eradicates Myeloproliferative Neoplasm-Sustaining Stem Cells
shortlist.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) arise from and are sustained by hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that acquire a driver mutation. Existing therapies fail to eliminate MPN HSCs, leaving allogeneic HSC transplantation (HSCT) as the only curative option. However, allogeneic HSCT non-selectively ablates both healthy and MPN HSCs, requiring donor stem-cell replacement and risking serious toxicities and death. MPN driver mutations in calreticulin (CALRmut) generate a shared C-terminal neopeptide unique to MPN cells that must be displayed at the cell surface in complex with the thrombopoietin receptor MPL to drive oncogenic signaling. These features make CALRmut an attractive target for selective immunotherapy. However, it is unknown whether MPN HSCs consistently display surface CALRmut to enable selective elimination in vivo via CALRmut targeting. We generated hAB2, a high-affinity CALRmut-specific humanized antibody, to use as the binding domain for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. We show that functional murine and human MPN HSCs express surface CALRmut that is reliably detected by AB2 in vitro and in vivo. We developed an MPN patient-derived tumor xenograft (PDTX) model to enable rigorous testing of human MPN HSC-directed therapies in vivo. hAB2 CAR-T cells selectively eliminate CALRmut MPN HSCs in PDTX, eradicating all detectable MPN-propagating function in serial transplantation assays, while preserving co-existing normal human and host hematopoiesis. These findings establish cell-surface CALRmut display as a therapeutically exploitable feature of MPN HSCs and support the feasibility of CALRmut-targeted, transplant-free immunotherapies with curative intent for CALRmut MPNs.

shortlist.title: Hepatic stellate cells remodel liver-resident CD8+ T cells and constrain immunosurveillance
shortlist.abstract: The liver constitutes a distinct immunological niche in which CD8+ T cells balance immune protection and tissue integrity. How chronic liver disease (CLD) remodels human liver–resident CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) create immunoinstructive fibrotic niches that regulate liver-resident CD8+ T cell differentiation, localization, and function. CD103-expressing liver-resident CD8+ T cells accumulate with increasing fibrosis severity and preferentially localize within collagen-rich scar tissue. HSC-derived and matrix-retained TGFβ promote acquisition of a residency program characterized by upregulation of CD103, ECM-binding integrins, and adhesion molecules. Despite their increased abundance, liver-resident CD8+ T cells in CLD exhibit impaired antigen-dependent effector function, increased inhibitory receptor expression, and a transcriptional program associated with T cell dysfunction. Importantly, responses to PMA/ionomycin remain intact, indicating preserved effector competence. Mechanistically, HSCs directly suppress antigen-specific liver-resident CD8+ T cell function, with partial restoration following PD-L1/PD-L2 blockade. These findings identify the fibrotic niche as a central regulator of liver-resident CD8+ T cells and reveal how fibrosis can limit local immunosurveillance.

shortlist.title: Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered ILC2s for targeted immune regulation
shortlist.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering has transformed cellular immunotherapies, yet whether CAR signaling can direct innate lymphoid cell functions for therapeutic applications has not been established. IL-10-producing ILC2s (ILC2 10 ) suppress pathogenic T cell responses in preclinical transplant models, making them attractive candidates for engineered regulatory cell therapies. Here we show that CD28 and CD3z are endogenous signaling modules with distinct expression kinetics in ILC2 activation. We engineered human ILC2 10 with CARs incorporating these domains and demonstrate that CAR activation via CD3z, CD28 or both induces robust proliferation and cytokine production, with each domain inducing distinct transcriptional programs, and combined CD3z and CD28 signaling uniquely inducing cytotoxic programs. In a xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease model, CAR-ILC2 10 more effectively inhibited human T cell engraftment and activity, displayed enhanced persistence and trafficked to sites of T cell-mediated injury. These findings establish CAR-ILC2s as programmable cellular therapies, with CAR signaling architecture shaping distinct ILC2 effector programs.

shortlist.title: The Economic Dynamics of City Structure: Evidence from Hiroshima’s Recovery
shortlist.abstract: We provide new theory and evidence on the resilience of internal city structure after a large shock, analyzing the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. Exploiting newly digitized data, we document that the city structure recovered within five years after the bombing. Our new dynamic quantitative model of internal city structure incorporates commuting, forward-looking location choices, migration frictions, agglomeration forces, and heterogeneous location fundamentals. Strong agglomeration forces in our estimated model explain Hiroshima's recovery, and we find an alternative equilibrium where the city center did not recover. These results highlight the role of agglomeration forces, multiple equilibria, and expectations in urban dynamics.

fundamentals.title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
fundamentals.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft matter physics is to describe materials, such as the living cytoplasm and tissues, that are simultaneously active, chemically driven, and exhibit long-lasting memory of mechanical stresses. Here, we construct a generalized hydrodynamic framework at finite wave vectors and frequencies that is applicable to nonequilibrium fluids with memory. By leveraging stationary correlation identities, we derive a generalized linear response theory for nonequilibrium steady states. This framework serves as a formal extension of Onsager’s regression hypothesis beyond thermal equilibrium. Our approach provides a direct pathway to derive transport coefficients from steady-state fluctuations without the traditional Mori-Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, generalizing the Green-Kubo relations to nonequilibrium systems. As a corollary, we derive two model-free variants of the nonequilibrium fluctuation-response relation for non-Markovian dynamics. These generalized relations explicitly capture the nonequilibrium circulating currents—an out-of-equilibrium signature that is invisible to conventional scalar formulations or frameworks that treat degrees of freedom independently. Applying our theory to chemically driven active fluids reveals the emergence of active viscoelastic memory, wherein chemical reaction cycles dynamically renormalize the macroscopic viscous response. Strikingly, this active memory can induce negative storage modulus at finite frequencies, a behavior absent in ordinary viscoelastic fluids. Our first-principles framework rigorously extends linear rheology to nonequilibrium systems and provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian dynamics across a broad range of biological and synthetic active matter.

fundamentals.title: Origin of Electride States and Their Responses under Pressure
fundamentals.abstract: Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. While existing theoretical frameworks, including the interstitial quasi-atom (ISQ) and electron-ion interaction (EII) models, have provided some useful phenomenological interpretations of the electride formation, the atomistic origin and the underlying physics of this charge redistribution remain unclear. Here, within a first-principles framework, we systematically study the evolution of electronic structures of compressed materials, using alkali metals as representative examples. By mapping symmetry-resolved electronic band states onto atomic orbitals, we find that (i) pressure-induced quantum confinement raises the energies of atomic orbitals due to enhanced kinetic energy and increased overlap between valence and core electrons, with the energy shift being larger for more delocalized s orbital than for more localized p and d orbitals; and (ii) this effect causes reordering of band states, making the electride states, which are composed of the interatomic hybridized pd orbitals, to progressively shift in energy below the s orbital states, leading to their occupation and the onset of electride behavior. This microscopic electronic-state picture clarifies the origin of the electride formation and provides a general framework for understanding the evolution of interstitial electronic states under compression across diverse materials.

fundamentals.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
fundamentals.abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. To examine the present scheme, we analyze the MAGNDATA database and find that 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. When the k index is fixed to its experimental value, the number of magnetic structures generated is on average about nine, also demonstrating the high efficiency of this scheme. Next, to quantitatively assess computational and predictive performance, we perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. fundamentals.title: Revealing temperature effects on sliding friction through many-body phonon dynamics
fundamentals.abstract: Despite centuries of research into friction through classical mechanics, the fundamental principles governing friction remain poorly understood, particularly its temperature-dependent nature. This study proposes a quantum theory that reexamines the fundamental principles of tribology. By employing the Feynman diagrammatic perturbation technique within the framework of quantum many-body theory, this study incorporates phonon-phonon interactions to capture the microscopic mechanisms of energy dissipation. The results demonstrate that the phonon radiation governed by harmonic interactions dominates energy dissipation at cryogenic temperatures. As temperature rises, phonon scattering governed by anharmonic interactions overtakes radiation as the primary dissipation mechanism. Further increases in temperature lead to greater damping and suppressed phonon excitation, thereby reducing energy dissipation. The competition among phonon radiation, phonon scattering, and phonon excitation gives rise to the non-monotonic temperature characteristics of friction. Notably, this non-monotonic temperature dependence is also reproduced by classical molecular dynamics simulations. This framework provides a unified understanding of disparate friction trends with temperature observed across different materials, offering insights into the fundamental mechanisms of frictional energy dissipation.

fundamentals.title: Universal small-scale fluctuation spectrum of Vlasov-Poisson turbulence
fundamentals.abstract: The thermal' fluctuation spectrum of the electric field arising due to particle noise in a quiescent Vlasov--Poisson plasma was derived in the 1960s. Here, we derive the universal fluctuation spectrum of the electric field, at Debye and sub-Debye scales, for a turbulent Vlasov--Poisson plasma. This spectrum arises from what is likely to be the final cascade’—a universal regime to be encountered at the extreme small-scale end of any turbulent cascade in a nearly collisionless plasma. The cascaded invariant is the generalized (negative) entropy C 2 , which is the quadratic Casimir invariant of the particle distribution function. C 2 cascades to small scales in both position and velocity space via both linear and nonlinear phase mixing, in such a way that the timescales associated with the two processes are `critically balanced’ at every scale. We construct a phenomenological scaling theory of the fluctuation spectrum of C 2 in ( k , s ) space—and hence of the electric field in k space—in arbitrary dimensions, where k and s are the spatial and velocity wavenumbers, respectively. The electric-field spectrum is sufficiently steep for the nonlinear mixing to be controlled by the largest-scale electric fluctuations, and so the C 2 cascade resembles the Batchelor cascade of a passive scalar, albeit in the kinetic phase space. The conclusions of our theory are corroborated by direct numerical simulations of a forced 1D-1V plasma. We predict that the cascade is ultimately terminated at the (spatial) wavenumber where the turbulent electric-field spectrum gives way to the fluctuation spectrum associated with discrete particle noise; this transition scale is set by the amplitude of the turbulent electric fields and the plasma parameter. fundamentals.title: First Principles Magnetohydrodynamical Theory for the Expanding Box Model: Effects on Expansion-induced Alfvén Wave Reflection
fundamentals.abstract: The expanding box model (EBM) has been widely employed to simulate multiscale plasma phenomena in the expanding solar wind by transforming the MHD equations to a comoving, noninertial frame. However, traditional formulations have suffered from historical ambiguity regarding the physical separation between the comoving and inertial reference frames, primarily arising from a classical approximation of an invariant magnetic field between them. To resolve this inconsistency, we reformulate the EBM from first principles using a fully covariant approach. Here, we model the expanding solar wind frame as an anisotropic expanding spacetime metric, allowing us to incorporate radial acceleration profiles and differential transverse expansion, ensuring that all physical fields are correctly transformed by expansion. We demonstrate that asymmetries identified in previous EBM-MHD literature are direct consequences of neglecting the tensorial scaling of the magnetic field. Our covariant treatment eliminates these residues, restoring symmetry in the comoving frame. Projecting our system back into the inertial frame clarifies the distinction between local plasma dynamics and plasma expansion, revealing the anisotropy of the Parker spiral as a geometric projection. Furthermore, linear wave analysis using Elsässer variables reveals that plasma expansion induces a low-frequency cutoff and geometric damping. Numerical integration demonstrates that expansion drives the reflection of Alfvén waves, generating counter-propagating modes primarily at low frequencies relative to the expansion rate, while high frequencies converge to the WKB approximation. fundamentals.title: Unramified Gromov–Witten and Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Mathematical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov–Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar–Vafa invariants for Fano curve classes and primitive Calabi–Yau classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar–Vafa invariants in these cases.

fundamentals.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
fundamentals.abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain’s proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is, for example, 1,2^(1/3),2^(-1/3) 1, 2 1 / 3, 2 − 1 / 3. This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature (2,2) (2, 2). The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature (3,3) (3, 3) in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on SL(2,Z)³ SL(2, R)³ SL (2, Z) 3 ∖ SL (2, R) 3 over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner’s measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

fundamentals.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits
fundamentals.abstract: We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits for orthogonal polynomials associated to a fixed measure on the real line and related systems. One of our results is that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has sine kernel asymptotics at a point ξ ξ, with regularly varying scaling, if and only if the orthogonality measure (spectral measure) has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is the Lebesgue measure. All previously known cases of sine kernel asymptotics, with absolutely continuous or singular measures, have regularly varying scaling. Our work is not limited to bulk universality; we show that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has a regularly varying scaling limit with a nontrivial limit kernel if and only if the orthogonality measure has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is not a point mass. The possible limit kernels correspond to homogeneous de Branges spaces; in particular, this equivalence completely characterizes several prominent universality classes such as hard edge universality, Fisher–Hartwig singularities, and jump discontinuities in the weights. A key ingredient in the proof is a new correspondence between measures and chains of de Branges spaces, not between Weyl functions and Hamiltonians. In order to handle limits with power law weights, this correspondence goes beyond the more common setting of Poisson-finite measures, and allows arbitrary power bounded measures.

fundamentals.title: The Limit of Nature: Thucydides and the Politics of Theory
fundamentals.abstract: This article reconsiders Thucydides’s role as a foundational theorist of human nature. Contrary to conventional readings, I argue that Thucydides approaches “nature” (physis) less as a universal principle of behavior than as a site of political and theoretical investigation. By distinguishing his authorial voice from those of his speakers, I demonstrate that his analysis consistently approaches human nature as a limit concept—a baseline and boundary of human capacity that emerges in moments of existential precarity—while introducing a more nuanced set of terms to describe the habitual behaviors of political groups. By nevertheless foregrounding the more robust and determinative concept of nature in moments of contentious deliberation, Thucydides encourages reflection on the political dynamics that generate essentialist theories in public discourse. His account thus serves as a helpful point of reference for thinking about how competitive, polarizing speech affects the substantive categories of political debate and analysis, and through them political action.

fundamentals.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
fundamentals.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SIREV and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.34770/6vgh-br25 and in the supplementary materials ( M180373_SM.zip [25.7MB]). fundamentals.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
fundamentals.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks. fundamentals.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
fundamentals.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
fundamentals.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive…

fundamentals.title: Constructive Ordinal Exponentiation
fundamentals.abstract: In classical mathematics, ordinal arithmetic is well-studied; constructively, addition and multiplication are well-known. We study constructive ordinal exponentiation, where ordinals are taken to be transitive, extensional, and wellfounded orders on sets. We present a negative result showing that general constructive ordinal exponentiation is impossible, but we suggest two definitions that come close. The first definition is abstract and solely motivated by the expected equations; this works as long as the base of the exponential is positive. The second definition is based on decreasing lists and can be seen as a constructive version of Sierpiński’s definition via functions with finite support; this requires the base to have a trichotomous least element. Whenever it makes sense to ask the question, the two constructions are equivalent, allowing us to prove algebraic laws, cancellation properties, and preservation of decidability of the exponential. The core ideas do not depend on any specific constructive set theory or type theory, but a concrete computer-checked mechanization using the Agda proof assistant is given in homotopy type theory.

fundamentals.title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
fundamentals.abstract: The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of existing techniques to compute derivatives of numerical solutions of differential equations. We first discuss the importance of gradients of solutions of differential equations in a variety of scientific domains. Second, we lay out and compare the mathematical foundations of the various approaches. Third, we cover computational considerations and explore the solutions available in modern scientific software. Last but not least, we provide best practices and recommendations for practitioners. We hope that this work accelerates the fusion of scientific models and data and fosters a modern approach to scientific modeling.
